basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING SEVEN DAYS FORFEITABLE BEREAVEMENT LEAVE WITH PAY IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS (Bereavement Leave Act of 2025)

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Provides Seven Days Forfeitable Bereavement Leave with Pay in Public and Private Sectors (bereavement Leave Act of 2025).
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Origin of Bill 464 (pending amendment to expand 'immediate family').
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Provides Seven Days Forfeitable Bereavement Leave with Pay in Public and Private Sectors (bereavement Leave Act of 2025).
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Ratified 2025-02-20; effectivity per the Act's final section (typically 15 days after Official Gazette publication).

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: Concrete and immediate: every employee in BARMM - government or private - gets seven (7) days of paid bereavement leave each year when a family member dies. If your employer operates in the region, this is a benefit you can claim on top of existing leave.
in_practice: 7 days, with pay, forfeitable (unused days don't carry over or convert to cash)
Applies to both public and private sector employees within BARMM
A pending bill (464) seeks to widen who counts as 'immediate family' - watch for amendments

for_specific_groups.Private-sector workers: Show this law (BAA 72) to HR if bereavement leave is refused
for_specific_groups.Employers: Update leave policies for BARMM-based staff
for_specific_groups.Grieving families: Time for burial rites and the mourning period without losing income

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All of BARMM unless the title names a specific place
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Laws take effect shortly after publication, but felt impact follows budgets, IRRs, and agency rollout - typically months, not days
what_you_can_do: Ask your municipal/barangay office or the implementing ministry how and when it will roll out where you live
Read the full text (PDF) on the Parliament's website or the Official Gazette of the Bangsamoro - the final sections say when it takes effect and who must act
If it isn't being implemented, raise it with your Member of Parliament or through the ministry's public assistance desk

key_terms_explained.BAA: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act - a regional law passed by the Bangsamoro Parliament, applying inside BARMM alongside national laws.
key_terms_explained.IRR: Implementing Rules and Regulations - the ministry-issued 'how-to' that turns a law's text into procedures; many laws only bite once the IRR is out.
key_terms_explained.GAA: General Appropriations Act - the annual budget law deciding how much each ministry and program gets.

benefits.headline: Seven paid days off, every year, when you lose a family member.

direct_benefits.benefit: Time for burial rites and the mourning period without losing income
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic entitlement upon a family member's death

limitations: Forfeitable: unused days don't carry over or convert to cash
Coverage of extended family may change - Bill 464 proposes widening 'immediate family'
